category_title: Autistic students who correctly process problems with matching gestures
minimal_context: The student is working on a worksheet to identify and classify geometric shapes by matching them with images of concrete objects.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please look at the first shape on the worksheet and find the matching object.

STUDENT: a cube. (Visually perceives the cardboard and selects the picture of the dice that resembles the shape)

TUTOR: Move on to the next shape on the page.

STUDENT: (Focuses on the picture of the rectangular box) Beams. (Uses a matching gesture to indicate the similarity of the shape) a pencil.

TUTOR: Now identify the tube from the images of the piggy bank or the football.

STUDENT: (Points hand gestures to the image of marbles and cans of milk, visually seeing the similarity of a circular shape instead of the requested objects)

options.A: The tutor allows the student to work at his own pace and take a break as desired.
options.B: The tutor asks the student to draw concrete objects, like a pencil or cap, resembling a beam.
options.C: The tutor provides the student with extra time to process the information and attempt to communicate.
options.D: The tutor issues the sanction of a verbal warning to the student during the worksheet activity.
